source: AstraZeneca press release: Efzimfotase alfa showed numerical improvement in Six-Minute (10-11-2026)

quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Efzimfotase alfa showed numerical improvement in Six-Minute (10-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HICKORY Phase III results for efzimfotase alfa (ALXN1850) in adolescents and adults with hypophosphatasia (HPP) not previously treated with Strensiq (n=84 vs placebo n=40): the trial did not achieve statistical significance on the primary endpoint but showed a numerical improvement, an LS mean difference of 17.05 metres in the Six-Minute Walk Test vs placebo at week 25 (p=0.1675); the company says the lack of statistical significance was largely due to better-than-expected results in the adult-onset HPP placebo group. The key secondary endpoint FACIT-Fatigue was nominally significant (LS mean difference 5.74, nominal p=0.0016) and other key secondary endpoints numerically favoured efzimfotase alfa. Paediatric-onset subgroup (n=60): 6MWT LS mean difference 35.6 metres (nominal p=0.0386); adult-onset subgroup (n=64): -2.70 (nominal p=0.8764). In a post hoc analysis 45.2% of treated patients achieved the minimum clinically important difference vs 30.0% on placebo (odds ratio 2.50, nominal p=0.0363). The open-label extension showed continued improvement up to week 49. Gianluca Pirozzi (Head of Development, Regulatory and Safety, Alexion): with the recently granted Priority Review in the US, 'we look forward to bringing this potential new therapy' to the HPP community. Results were presented at the 2026 ASBMR Annual Meeting.
quarterly_data.figure: 6MWT +17.05 metres vs placebo (p=0.1675, not statistically significant); paediatric-onset subgroup +35.6 metres (nominal p=0.0386)
